text: Studies comparing superslow training to traditional training whereby both conditions are performed to volitional fatigue have not shown a benefit from higher TUTs; in fact, evidence indicates training in a traditional fashion produces superior hypertrophy despite a substantially lower TUT (221). A caveat to these findings is that the higher TUT in the superslow condition was at the expense of a much lower intensity of load. How these variables interact with one another to affect muscle growth is not clear.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 4: Role of Resistance Training Variables in Hypertrophy
